dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite-component field Q and flux F, every real a, b, and s satisfy both interval integrability of x ↦ Q(x,s) and differentiability at s of τ ↦ ∫_a^b Q(x,τ) dx, with derivative F(Q(a,s)) − F(Q(b,s)).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Assumes the integral balance law and spatial interval integrability at every real time, not just the selected time t.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps speed to the one-by-one real matrix whose sole entry is speed.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The coefficient matrix is [speed], with no sign or nonzero restriction.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps a square matrix A and a state v to the matrix-vector product Av.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the flux as multiplication by [speed].

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For scalar q, this is exactly LocalDef007 q speed x t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The second conclusion asserts scalar time and space derivatives satisfying the transport equation.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Embeds q(x,s) into the function on Fin 1 taking the value q(x,s) at its unique index.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Converts the scalar field into a one-component vector field without changing its values.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real scalar multiplication on a function space ι → Real is jointly continuous.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the continuity structure needed for derivatives of the embedded field; it imposes no hypothesis on q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real normed vector space E, there exist u,v in E such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative u at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative v at x, and u + speed • v = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: At each x the conclusion provides scalar derivative witnesses and their exact equation; these witnesses may depend on x and the fixed parameters.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real scalar multiplication in any real normed vector space is jointly continuous.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the derivative predicates in LocalDef007; the target specializes the space to Real.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommMonoid.toAddMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the additive monoid underlying a commutative additive monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Preserves the real addition used in module structures.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.id
dependency_coverage.meaning: Makes a commutative semiring an algebra over itself using the identity algebra map and multiplication as scalar multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Real scalar multiplication on Real is ordinary multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.toSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the scalar multiplication of an algebra.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Uses the self-algebra action of Real in the continuity structures.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction requiring both propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires both final conclusions, both clauses of the integral law, and all clauses of the derivative-witness conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: Continuous
dependency_coverage.meaning: Continuity of a function between the specified topological spaces.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires the residual x ↦ qt(x) + fluxx(x) to be continuous on all of Real.

dependency_coverage.name: DenselyNormedField.toNontriviallyNormedField
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains a densely normed field as a nontrivially normed field.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the real scalar field structure required by HasDerivAt.

dependency_coverage.name: DistribMulAction.toMulAction
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the monoid action underlying a distributive multiplicative action.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Preserves the real scalar action used on vector coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: DivisionSemiring.toSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the semiring underlying a division semiring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies ordinary real addition and multiplication for module construction.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Equality of two objects of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The flux equality is equality of functions on Fin 1; the transport residual equals scalar zero exactly.

dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the semiring and division operations of a field as a semifield.

dependency_coverage.name: Module.toDistribMulAction

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toSemigroup

binders: Universally quantify a function q: Real × Real → Real, written q(x,s), with the first argument serving as space and the second as time.
Universally quantify speed c ∈ Real and a selected time t ∈ Real.
Universally quantify qt, qx, fluxx: Real → V, where V is the real vector space Fin 1 → Real.
In the integral-balance assumption, a, b, and s range independently over all real numbers; its time variable s is independent of the selected time t.
In the derivative assumptions and final transport conclusion, x ranges over all real numbers. In the integrability and interchange assumptions, a and b range independently over all real numbers.
In the first conclusion, state ranges over all of V; its output index ranges over Fin 1.
For each x in the second conclusion, there exist real numbers u and v, chosen within that x's scope, representing the time and space derivatives at (x,t).
hypotheses: Write Q(x,s)(i)=q(x,s) for i ∈ Fin 1, A(i,j)=c, and F(state)=A state. For every a,b,s ∈ Real, x ↦ Q(x,s) is interval integrable with respect to real volume from a to b, and τ ↦ ∫_a^b Q(x,τ) dx has derivative F(Q(a,s))−F(Q(b,s)) at s.
For every x ∈ Real, τ ↦ Q(x,τ) has derivative qt(x) at t.
For every x ∈ Real, ξ ↦ Q(ξ,t) has derivative qx(x) at x.
For every x ∈ Real, ξ ↦ F(Q(ξ,t)) has derivative fluxx(x) at x.
For every a,b ∈ Real, qt is interval integrable from a to b with respect to real volume.
For every a,b ∈ Real, fluxx is interval integrable from a to b with respect to real volume.
For every a,b ∈ Real, τ ↦ ∫_a^b Q(x,τ) dx has derivative ∫_a^b qt(x) dx at the selected time t.
The function x ↦ qt(x)+fluxx(x) from Real to V is continuous.
conclusions: For every state ∈ V, F(state) is the function on Fin 1 whose value at every index is c·state(0).
For every x ∈ Real, there exist u,v ∈ Real such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative u at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative v at x, and u+c·v=0.
mathematical_definitions: Fin 1 is the singleton index set {0}; V=Real^{Fin 1} is a one-dimensional real vector space with pointwise arithmetic and its usual product topology and norm.
Q is the scalar-to-vector embedding Q(x,s)(0)=q(x,s).
A is the one-by-one matrix [c], and F(state)(i)=Σ_{j∈Fin 1} A(i,j)state(j).
All integrals use real Lebesgue volume. The oriented integral ∫_a^b f is the integral over (a,b] minus the integral over (b,a].
Interval integrability means integrability on both (a,b] and (b,a]; this handles either ordering of endpoints.

A derivative assertion means existence of the ordinary two-sided real-variable derivative with the specified value. For V-valued functions it is equivalently the assertion for their sole real coordinate.
The scalar transport predicate at (x,t) means existence of the two partial derivatives there and the equation ∂q/∂t(x,t)+c·∂q/∂x(x,t)=0.
The existential witnesses in the conclusion are not syntactically identified with the input functions qt and qx, but uniqueness of derivatives forces u=qt(x)(0) and v=qx(x)(0).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any real scalar field q(x,s), any real constant speed c, any real time t, and any one-component derivative fields qt, qx, and fluxx, assume the following. At every real time s, the embedded field Q is integrable on every bounded spatial interval, and the time derivative of its oriented interval integral equals the flux at the left endpoint minus the flux at the right endpoint, where the flux is multiplication by the one-by-one matrix [c]. At time t, Q has time derivative qt(x) and space derivative qx(x) at every x, and its flux has space derivative fluxx(x). Both qt and fluxx are integrable on every bounded interval. Differentiating each interval integral at t gives the interval integral of qt, and qt+fluxx is continuous in space. Then both of the following hold: the flux of every one-component state is the one-component vector with value c times its coordinate at 0; and at every real spatial point x, q has scalar time and space derivatives at (x,t) whose values u and v satisfy u+c·v=0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The target is scalar and one-dimensional in both space and state. The more general finite-index and normed-space dependencies do not make this target a theorem about arbitrary systems or spatial dimensions.
Space and time range over all real numbers. There is no restriction to nonnegative time, a bounded spatial domain, or an interior subset.

Speed is one fixed real constant, independent of space and time, with no positivity or nonzero assumption. At speed zero, the scalar equation reduces to vanishing time derivative while spatial differentiability remains required.

The integral balance and integrability of Q are assumed at every real time. The additional pointwise derivative, derivative-integrability, interchange, and residual-continuity assumptions concern the selected time t.
The conclusion concerns every x at the selected time t. It does not assert that the additional regularity assumptions hold at every time.
The time-derivative/interchange condition is explicitly assumed for every interval; it is not derived from the other regularity hypotheses by the proposition.
Only the sum qt+fluxx is assumed continuous. Separate continuity of qt, qx, or fluxx, joint continuity of partial derivatives, and global C1 regularity are not explicitly assumed.
The conclusion is pointwise and asserts actual derivative existence. It is not merely an almost-everywhere, distributional, or weak transport equation.
No ordering a≤b is required. When a=b the integral statements are trivial, but quantification over all endpoint pairs prevents the interval hypotheses from reducing to that degenerate case.
Fin 1 is inhabited, so neither the state-coordinate assertions nor the matrix sum are vacuous through an empty index set.

Integrability is required on each bounded interval, not over the whole real line. The explicit interval-integrability hypotheses ensure the relevant integrals are genuine integrals rather than relying on totalized values for nonintegrable functions.
The first conclusion is an algebraic consequence of the flux definition alone. The statement does not derive or identify an unknown physical flux from the integral balance law.
This is a conditional theorem, not an existence or uniqueness theorem for solutions. No initial data, boundary conditions, characteristic formula, or converse implication is encoded.

For data failing any assumption the implication makes no claim about the transport equation. The assumptions are not inherently contradictory: the zero field with zero derivative fields satisfies them for every speed and selected time.
